flashcards.q: Define weak stationarity and state when an AR(1) is stationary.
flashcards.a: E[x_t]=mu constant, Var(x_t)=sigma^2 constant, Cov(x_t,x_s)=g(|t-s|) depends only on lag. AR(1) x_t=phi*x_{t-1}+e_t is weakly stationary iff |phi|<1; at phi=1 it is a random walk with variance n*sigma^2 after n steps.

flashcards.q: What did Granger-Newbold (1974) show about regressing independent random walks on each other?
flashcards.a: Nominal 5% t-tests rejected ~70-76% of the time; under a unit-root null the t/F statistics diverge (Phillips 1986), so level regressions between trending series are meaningless regardless of R^2. Heuristic: worry when R^2 > Durbin-Watson.

flashcards.q: Write the ADF regression, its null/alternative, and the 5% critical value (constant-only case).
flashcards.a: dx_t = a + g*x_{t-1} + sum b_i dx_{t-i} + e. H0: g=0 (unit root); H1: g<0 (mean reversion). Critical values -3.43/-2.86/-2.57 at 1/5/10% come from the Dickey-Fuller distribution (functional of Brownian motion), NOT t-tables.

flashcards.q: Why pair ADF with KPSS? What are their nulls?
flashcards.a: ADF H0 = unit root, KPSS H0 = stationarity (reversed). ADF's low power against persistent-stationary alternatives (phi~0.9 ARs often fail to reject) means classification is reliable only when they agree: stationary iff ADF rejects AND KPSS fails to reject.

flashcards.q: Give the signature signs of overdifferencing and what breaks mechanically.
flashcards.a: Lag-1 autocorrelation pushed near -0.5, inflated variance vs once-differenced data, MA coefficient hugging -1 (non-invertible unit-root MA), oscillating forecasts. Differencing a trend-stationary series manufactures an artificial MA(1) with theta->-1.

flashcards.q: State the identification signatures for AR(p), MA(q), ARMA.
flashcards.a: AR(p): ACF decays geometrically, PACF cuts off after p. MA(q): ACF cuts off after q, PACF decays. ARMA(p,q): both tail off. Seasonal spikes at lags m,2m signal SARIMA terms. Plots propose; AIC/BIC + residual diagnostics dispose.

flashcards.q: Set up Yule-Walker estimation and its bias property.
flashcards.a: Match theoretical to sample autocovariances: Toeplitz system Gamma_p*phi = gamma solved via Durbin-Levinson in O(p^2). Bias follows sample ACF downward bias: Hurwicz E[phi_hat] ~ phi - (1+3phi)/T (AR(1)), e.g. phi=0.9, T=100 -> ~-0.037. MLE beats it at small T.

flashcards.q: State Wold's theorem and why it licenses ARMA models.
flashcards.a: Any weakly stationary process = deterministic component + infinite MA of uncorrelated innovations. So finite-order ARMA approximates any stationary process arbitrarily well - the justification for staying in a small parametric family.

flashcards.q: Give the stationarity triangle conditions for AR(2) and what complex roots mean.
flashcards.a: z^2 - phi1*z - phi2 roots outside unit circle <=> phi1+phi2<1, phi2-phi1<1, |phi2|<1. Complex conjugate roots = damped oscillation (stochastic cycle); modulus sets decay rate, angle sets pseudo-period. Roots ON circle = unit roots.

flashcards.q: What is the airline model and why is it the default monthly baseline?
flashcards.a: ARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)_12 on log levels: d=1 removes stochastic trend, D=1 removes evolving seasonality, two MA(1)s smooth local deviations. Two interpretable parameters, robust, fits a huge share of monthly business series (Box-Jenkins airline data).

flashcards.q: How does forecast uncertainty grow with horizon for AR(1) vs random walk vs MA(q)?
flashcards.a: AR(1): var_h = sigma^2*(1-phi^(2h))/(1-phi^2), saturates at unconditional variance (mean reversion caps it). Random walk: var ~ h*sigma^2, fans out forever. MA(q): flat intervals beyond q steps (forecast collapses to mean). Software bands usually ignore parameter estimation error - bootstrap for honesty.

flashcards.q: Compare STL and X-13ARIMA-SEATS and name the finance-specific caveat about adjustment.
flashcards.a: STL (Cleveland 1990): loess-based, evolving seasonality, robust to outliers, no native forecasting. X-13ARIMA-SEATS: statutory standard, RegARIMA calendar/outlier pre-adjustment, model-based extraction, revises factors as data arrives. Caveats: adjusting first distorts variance and embeds assumptions downstream users inherit; adjusted series carry no honest confidence intervals.

flashcards.q: AIC vs BIC for ARIMA order selection - formulas and philosophical difference?
flashcards.a: AIC=-2logL+2k targets best out-of-sample forecast accuracy; BIC=-2logL+k*ln(T) penalizes complexity harder as T grows and targets recovery of the true order. They can disagree: BIC picks sparser models; AIC asymptotically efficient for prediction.

flashcards.q: Why log prices before differencing, and what does integer differencing cost quants?
flashcards.a: diff(log price) = simple returns: stabilizes variance and gives interpretable units. Cost: d=1 amputates long memory - slow hyperbolic ACF decay (Hurst>0.5) vanishes, destroying predictive signal; fractional differencing (ARFIMA, d~0.1-0.45) achieves stationarity while preserving maximal memory (Lopez de Prado).
